ingredients: Torte: ½ cup margarine or butter
Torte: ½ cup white granulated sugar
Glaze: 5 teaspoons boiling water, plus more if needed
Caramel: ½ cup heavy whipping cream
Topping: prepared chocolate glaze, caramel sauce, optional chocolate curls, and ½ cup chopped pecans
steps: Preheat oven to 325°F. Grease a 9x3-inch springform pan.
For the torte, melt chocolate chips and ½ cup butter in a two-quart saucepan over medium heat. Cool 5 minutes. Stir in flour, then egg yolks until smooth.
Whip egg whites until foamy, then beat in granulated sugar 1 tablespoon at a time until soft peaks form. Fold in chocolate mixture.
Spread in prepared pan and bake 35–40 minutes until dry and cracked on top. Cool 10 minutes.

For the glaze, melt unsweetened chocolate and 1 teaspoon butter over low heat. Blend in powdered sugar and 5 teaspoons boiling water; add more boiling water ½ teaspoon at a time to a drizzling consistency.
For the caramel sauce, bring brown sugar, cream, corn syrup, 1 tablespoon butter and cinnamon to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly. Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered 5 minutes.

For the curls, warm the chocolate bar for about 15 minutes. Place on waxed paper and pull a vegetable peeler firmly across its flattest side. Transfer curls with a toothpick to a wax-lined cookie sheet.
Run a knife around the cake and remove the pan sides. Cool completely and place on a serving plate. Spread with glaze, drizzle with caramel sauce, and garnish with curls and pecans.

ingredients: ½ cup (60 g/2.1 oz) unsweetened cocoa powder
¼ cup plus 2 tablespoons (90 ml/3 fl oz) hot brewed coffee
⅔ cup (80 g/2.8 oz) powdered sugar
1 oz (28 g) kirsch, chocolate brandy, or coffee liqueur
steps: Whisk cocoa powder, coffee and salt in a medium bowl to the consistency of melted chocolate, adding another tablespoon of coffee if too thick. Set aside.
Whip cream in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium-high for 1 minute.
Add powdered sugar and whip another minute.
Add kirsch and the coffee-cocoa mixture; whip on high until stiff peaks form, about another minute.
Spoon into a piping bag or plastic bag, twist closed, and snip off one corner about ½ inch up.
Arrange chocolate cups on serving plates, using a dollop of mousse underneath if they will not sit flat. Pipe mousse into the cups.
Shave chocolate over the filled cups with a vegetable peeler and top each with a cherry.

ingredients: 4 ounces (110 g / 2 small tins) anchovy fillets or anchovy paste
1–3 fresh or dried hot chile peppers, deseeded and finely chopped
1 can (6 ounces / 170 g) pitted black or kalamata olives, quartered
1 lb (454 g) dry spaghetti or linguine
steps: Fill a large pot with water, add a handful of salt, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Heat 4 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onions and cook until soft, stirring occasionally without burning.
Add garlic and anchovies; cook no more than 1 minute, stirring to break up anchovies.
Add capers, chiles, olives, tomatoes, pepper and 1 tablespoon salt. Bring to a boil, reduce to medium-low and simmer uncovered 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Taste and adjust salt.
While sauce simmers, boil pasta until al dente, about 12 minutes. Drain in a colander and return to the pot.
Pour sauce over pasta and toss over low heat until coated. Remove from heat, top with parsley and remaining 1 tablespoon oil, and serve hot.
